Deep summer ploughing to expose disease to sun; good drainage.
Fertilize based on soil health card.

Monitoring: Check for brownish, irregular semi circles on sheath, stem and leaves.
Check for whitish cottony growth (mycelium) on leaf sheath/blade near the water line.
Check for minute ball like structure (sclerotia) on leaf sheath near the water line.
Be extra vigilent 30 to 35 days after transplanting and onward.
If around 5% of plants show symptoms use then consider direct control actions.
Direct Control: Pseudomonas fluorescens at a rate of 2.5 kg/Ha with 500
L of water when threshold reached.
Drain off standing water from the infected field.
Carbendazim at a rate of 0.1% at appearance of disease or 250-300 gm/acre with 150 litres of water.
Restrictions: Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) is recommended while using chemical pesticides.
WHO U (unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use).
Maximum of two applications with 15 day interval.
Be careful as can kill important pollinators such as honeybees.
